job.title: Nurse Practitioner
job.description:
About RWR Health & Nurse Practitioners
At RWR Health, we connect exceptional healthcare professionals with organisations that genuinely align with their career goals, values and lifestyle.

We take the time to understand what you're looking for and connect you with opportunities where you can develop professionally, feel supported and make a meaningful difference to the communities you serve.

We are currently looking to connect with a Nurse Practitioner to join a supportive and community-focused Primary Care team in South Auckland.

This is an opportunity to work within an established General Practice environment, providing high-quality, patient-centred care while working alongside an experienced multidisciplinary team.

The Opportunity
We are open to 3 or 5 days per week, providing flexibility to find a working pattern that suits your lifestyle and professional goals.

You'll work within a predominantly Māori and Pasifika community, providing accessible and culturally responsive Primary Care to patients and their whānau.

This could be an excellent opportunity for an NP who already has experience working within these communities, or someone with a genuine passion for developing their understanding and capability in Māori and Pasifika healthcare.

Why This Role Stands Out
  • 3 or 5 days per week to support your lifestyle
  • Work within a predominantly Māori & Pasifika community
  • Join a supportive and collaborative Primary Care environment
  • Deliver meaningful, patient-centred healthcare within your scope
  • Opportunity for continued professional development and career growth
Your Clinical Environment
You'll be part of a team that values collaboration, respect and quality patient care.

The practice has a strong focus on supporting the health and wellbeing of its local community, with culturally responsive care playing an important role in how services are delivered.

You'll have the opportunity to build strong relationships with patients and whānau while contributing to accessible and equitable healthcare.

About You
We're looking for a Nurse Practitioner who brings strong clinical skills, excellent communication and a genuine commitment to patient-centred care.

You will ideally have:
  • Current Nurse Practitioner registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand
  • A current practising certificate
  • Experience within Primary Care 
  • Excellent clinical assessment and decision-making skills
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • A collaborative approach to multidisciplinary healthcare
  • A commitment to culturally responsive and equitable healthcare
  • An understanding of the health needs of Māori and Pasifika communities
  • A compassionate and patient-focused approach
  • Legal eligibility to work in New Zealand
Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is clinically capable, compassionate, community-minded and passionate about making a difference.

Your Development
You'll be joining an environment where professional development and continued learning are encouraged.

Whether you're an experienced Nurse Practitioner or looking to further establish yourself within Primary Care, this opportunity provides the support and clinical environment to continue developing your career.

Ready to Explore What's Next?
If you're a Nurse Practitioner looking for a supportive Primary Care environment, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to make a genuine difference within a Māori and Pasifika community, I'd love to hear from you.

Not quite right for you?
Know someone who could be a great fit? We offer a $500 cash referral bonus for successful introductions.

Principal GP & Primary Care Recruiter

job.title: General Practitioner (Fellow)
job.description:
About RWR Health & General Practitioners
At RWR Health, we connect GPs with organisations that genuinely align with what they want from their careers.

Whether you're looking to develop your clinical skills, find a supportive General Practice environment, or have longer-term ambitions around practice ownership, our role is to understand what matters to you and connect you with the right opportunity.

We are proud to be representing an established Primary Care organisation in South Auckland that offers something particularly exciting for GP Fellows.

The Opportunity
We are looking for a General Practitioner Fellow to join a supportive and community-focused Primary Care team.

The position is open to 3 or 4 days per week, providing flexibility while you continue to develop your clinical career.

What makes this opportunity different is the potential to build something longer term.
If ownership or Leadership is something you've considered for your future, this is a genuine conversation you can have from the outset.

The organisation is open to supporting the right GP Fellow to progress towards an ownership opportunity, potentially within their first year.

You'll be joining a team where your contribution is valued, your clinical development is supported, and there is scope to build a long-term future.

Why This Role Stands Out
  • Genuine pathway to part ownership within 12 months
  • 3 or 4 days per week, offering flexibility around your lifestyle
  • Join a community-focused practice with a strong Māori and Pasifika patient population
  • Develop your career within a supportive and collaborative Primary Care team
  • Flexibility to work both in Clinic and Virtually from Home if you are looking for a blend. 
Your Clinical Environment
This is a community-focused General Practice.

The team places importance on accessible, patient-centred healthcare and understands the importance of providing care that is culturally responsive and relevant to the communities they serve.

For a GP Fellow who has experience working with Māori and Pasifika communities — or someone with a genuine passion for developing their understanding and capability in this area — this provides an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution while continuing to grow clinically.

Your Development As a GP Fellow, you'll have the opportunity to continue building your confidence and capability within General Practice while working alongside an experienced and supportive team.

You'll be encouraged to develop your:
  • Clinical decision-making and consultation skills
  • Confidence managing a diverse patient population
  • Understanding of culturally responsive healthcare
  • Long-term Primary Care career goals
  • Leadership and service development capability
  • Broader understanding of the operational side of General Practice
And if your longer-term goal is practice ownership or Leadership, you'll have the opportunity to explore what that could look like from an early stage.

About You
We're interested in speaking with GP Fellows who are looking for more than just their next clinical role.

You may be:
  • A GP Fellow looking for a supportive environment to continue your development
  • Interested in building a long-term career within Primary Care
  • Exploring practice ownership as a future goal
  • Feeling ready to take that step towards GP Leadership
  • Passionate about working with Māori and Pasifika communities
  • Committed to providing patient-centred and culturally responsive care
  • A strong communicator who enjoys working collaboratively
  • Looking for flexibility around your working week
You'll also hold the relevant MCNZ registration and eligibility to work in New Zealand.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is clinically capable, community-minded, curious and motivated to build a long-term future in General Practice.

job.title: Physiotherapist
job.description:
About the Organisation
 
Our client provides specialist palliative care to people living with life-limiting illness across the Hutt Valley.

Their focus is on helping people live as well as possible - maintaining independence, function and quality of life while supporting patients and whānau through changing and complex health needs.
 
About the Job

Working across an 8 bed inpatient unit and in the community, you'll provide physiotherapy assessment, rehabilitation and support throughout the palliative care journey. You'll work closely with the Occupational Therapist and wider multidisciplinary team to:
  • Assess mobility, function, fatigue, breathlessness and physical needs.
  • Provide rehabilitation and mobility interventions based on individual goals.
  • Recommend equipment and provide manual handling advice.
  • Support patients to maintain independence and quality of life.
  • Contribute to family meetings and complex care discussions.
  • Provide education to whānau, carers, staff and other health professionals.
There is also scope to help develop the palliative rehabilitation space, contributing to education, service development and innovative rehabilitation initiatives.

The role is 20 - 24 hours per week, preferably across three days. There is flexibility around how these are structured, although you'll need to attend at least two 8.30am MDT meetings each week.
 
About You

You don't need to be a palliative care specialist. We're looking for an experienced Physiotherapist with strong clinical foundations, sound judgement and the confidence to work with a good degree of autonomy.

Your background might be in community rehabilitation, older persons' health, neurology, respiratory, oncology, complex care or another area involving people with changing health needs. You'll bring:
  • NZ registration and a current APC.
  • Ideally 3+ years' physiotherapy experience within New Zealand.
  • Strong generalist assessment and rehabilitation skills.
  • Confidence working autonomously and collaboratively within an MDT.
  • Excellent communication and cultural capability.
  • The maturity and resilience to support people and whānau experiencing life-limiting illness.
Palliative care experience is welcomed but not essential - training, supervision and support are available to develop this expertise.
 
What's On Offer?
  • $90,000 - $110,000 per annum, pro rata for hours worked.
  • 20 - 24 hours per week with flexibility.
  • A collaborative multidisciplinary environment.
  • Supervision, in-service education and structured palliative care development.
  • Scope to contribute to rehabilitation innovation and service development.
  • Meaningful work where physiotherapy can make a genuine difference to how people live.
APPLY NOW
 
If you're an experienced Physiotherapist looking for meaningful work and the opportunity to develop your skills in palliative care, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply via the APPLY NOW link.
 
For a copy of the position description or a confidential conversation, contact Jeanette Rendle, Director - RWR Health Lower North Island, on 027 705 7079.

job.title: Clinical Service Leader
job.description:
Are you an experienced Registered Psychologist with a background in harmful sexual behaviour or forensic practice, looking to step into a senior clinical leadership role without moving away from clinical practice?
We are seeking a Clinical Service Lead to provide clinical leadership, guidance and oversight across services throughout Northland, Auckland, Waikato and Tauranga.

You'll be a senior clinical resource for experienced clinicians providing case consultation, reviewing clinical practice, supporting complex decision-making and helping develop the quality and consistency of the Adult Services programme.

The opportunity
Reporting to the Clinical Director, you'll provide clinical leadership across a geographically dispersed team while remaining connected to practice yourself.

A significant part of your role will involve supporting clinicians with their clinical work. You'll hold regular monthly one-to-one meetings, review caseloads, provide guidance around complex presentations and risk, and ensure assessment and intervention approaches remain clinically robust.
You'll also have an opportunity to influence the ongoing development of the Adult Services programme, clinical frameworks and ways of working.

The position description places approximately 60% of the role's focus on clinical leadership, with a further 20% dedicated to clinical work, alongside learning and development and stakeholder engagement.

What you'll be doing
  • Providing clinical leadership and guidance across Adult Services in Northland, Auckland, Waikato and Tauranga
  • Holding monthly clinical 1:1s with clinicians, including reviewing caseloads and providing case consultation
  • Providing specialist guidance on complex presentations, risk, assessment and intervention
  • Reviewing and approving assessment and intervention reports to support consistently high standards of practice
  • Supporting the effective triage of new referrals
  • Providing clinical direction around complex cases, ethical considerations and client risk
  • Supporting clinicians working with specialist populations, including clients with intellectual disabilities and women
  • Contributing to the development and refinement of Safe Network's Adult Services programme
  • Supporting clinical onboarding, capability development and training
  • Contributing to clinical policies, programmes and best-practice frameworks
  • Maintaining a level of hands-on clinical practice, including assessment and therapeutic intervention
  • Building collaborative relationships with referrers, agencies and other sector stakeholders
  • Travelling across the Northern Region as required
The position has no direct reports, so your leadership comes through your clinical expertise, credibility, guidance and ability to positively influence practice.

What we're looking for
We're particularly interested in hearing from experienced psychologists who have worked within harmful sexual behaviour services or forensic environments.
You'll need to be comfortable with some of the more complex presentations encountered within Adult Services and bring well-developed expertise across assessment, risk and therapeutic intervention.
You'll ideally bring:
  • Full registration as a Psychologist with NZPB
  • Relevant clinical experience 
  • Strong experience delivering clinical assessments within harmful sexual behaviour or forensic settings
  • Expertise across harmful sexual behaviour assessment and intervention
  • Experience with systemic interventions and group work
  • Strong risk assessment, formulation and clinical decision-making capability
  • Previous clinical leadership experience
  • Confidence providing consultation, feedback and guidance to experienced clinicians
  • The ability to review complex clinical information and provide clear direction
  • Strong written skills and experience producing or reviewing high-quality clinical reports
  • An ability to build credibility and effective working relationships across geographically dispersed services
  • A collaborative, thoughtful and culturally responsive approach to practice
  • Flexibility to undertake some regional travel
Experience supporting specialist populations, including people with intellectual disabilities would also be valuable.

With a strong focus on creating safer outcomes for individuals, whānau and communities.

This is an opportunity to bring your expertise into a role where you can have a broader clinical impact – supporting other experienced practitioners, strengthening clinical practice and contributing to the future development of specialist Adult Services – without taking on traditional staff-management responsibilities.

What's in it for you?
Alongside the professional opportunity, this role offers a strong benefits package including:
  • Competitive Salary
  • Health insurance
  • Income protection insurance
  • Critical care cover
  • Annual professional registration
  • Monthly professional supervision
  • Car parking
If you're an experienced Registered Psychologist from an HSB, forensic or closely aligned specialist background and want to move into a role where your clinical expertise can influence practice across an entire service, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now or get in touch for a confidential conversation about the opportunity. Robbie McKenzie, Agency Director, RWR Health
P: 027 519 4993
E: robbiem@rwrhealth.co.nz
W: www.rwrhealth.copm

job.title: Service Delivery Manager- 10k relocation allowance to Taranaki
job.description:
About the organisation

Our client is an established community based disability support provider operating across the North Island. Their focus is simple but important - supporting disabled people to live the lives they choose, within their own communities.

Values-led and people-focused, they are passionate about delivering genuinely person-centred services and building capable, well-supported teams.

About the Job

Based in New Plymouth, you'll lead two 24/7 residential services. The people supported, and their needs, are different, but the goal is the same: high-quality, person-centred support that enables people to live the lives they choose.

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading, coaching and developing frontline teams, creating a culture where Support Workers feel safe, valued and confident, while managing performance, recruitment and development.
  • Overseeing daily service delivery, including rosters, staffing, resources, incidents, risk, health and safety and quality requirements.
  • Building strong relationships with the people supported, family/whānau, NASC, clinical teams, funders and community partners.
  • Working alongside the General Manager to ensure services meet contractual and legislative requirements while identifying opportunities to strengthen and grow services.
Who are we looking for?

We'd like to hear from people who bring:
  • Experience within disability, health, mental health or social services
  • Leadership experience with frontline or community-based teams
  • Confidence working around complex needs and behaviours
  • Strong coaching, mentoring and people-management capability
  • Experience managing performance and navigating challenging conversations
  • The ability to build constructive relationships with family/whānau while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries
  • Confidence working with external stakeholders and navigating the wider disability support system
  • Sound judgement, resilience and the ability to remain calm when situations become complex
  • A genuine commitment to the rights, choice and independence of disabled people.
  • Appropriate Police and Oranga Tamariki clearances (or ability to gain)
  • A full driver's licence.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification (minimum Level 7) e.g. bachelors in management, nursing, social services, psychology etc
Don't tick every box? We'd still like to hear from you.

Our client recognises that the right person may not come with every piece of experience already in place. You could be an experienced disability leader, a Team Leader ready for greater responsibility, or someone from an adjacent health or social service environment with strong transferable experience. What you will need is drive, curiosity, compassion and a willingness to learn. You'll be an advocate, a problem solver and someone prepared to step in when your team needs you.

What's on offer?
Alongside genuinely meaningful work, our client offers:
  • Salary of $80,000-$110,000, depending on experience
  • Five weeks' annual leave
  • Monday - Friday business hours
  • A shared after hours and weekend on call roster approximately once every couple of months
  • Support from an experienced local Service Delivery Manager
  • Access to specialist HR, quality and organisational support
  • Relocation assistance of up to $10,000 for the right candidate
  • An opportunity to help strengthen and grow disability services in Taranaki.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
About the organisation

Our client is a well-established kaupapa Māori organisation that has been working alongside whānau for 40 years.

Based in Hastings, they deliver an extensive range of health, social, education, housing and community services across the region. Everything they do is underpinned by their values of Kaitiakitanga, Whakamana, Kotahitanga and Whanaungatanga.

You don’t need to arrive fluent in te reo Māori or already know everything about working within a kaupapa Māori organisation. What is important is that you are genuinely open to learning, willing to participate and understand that relationships come first.

About the job

Reporting to the CFO, this is a hands on Finance Manager role leading the day to day finance function and a team covering financial accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable and cash management.

There is plenty of complexity to keep an experienced finance professional interested. This organisation operates across multiple entities and services, with varied funding and contractual arrangements and a high volume of transactions. You’ll oversee the month end cycle, financial reporting, cashflow, reconciliations, budgeting and forecasting, compliance and audit preparation, while ensuring the fundamentals are done accurately and on time.

Just as importantly, you’ll get out from behind the spreadsheet. You’ll build relationships with Service Delivery Managers, help them understand their financials, provide practical advice and translate the numbers into information that helps people make better decisions.

Having invested in its finance systems, this organisation is now well positioned to keep improving how technology, systems and processes are used. There is a real appetite for curiosity and continuous improvement - looking at what can be streamlined, automated or simply done better.

You’ll be responsible for:
  • Leading, coaching and developing the finance team, creating clear expectations while encouraging greater confidence, curiosity and accountability.
  • Taking ownership of core financial operations including AP, AR, cashflow, general ledger, reconciliations and month end.
  • Preparing accurate and meaningful management reporting, variance analysis and financial insights across multiple entities.
  • Supporting budgeting, forecasting, consolidated reporting, audit preparation, GST and other compliance requirements.
  • Partnering with operational managers to understand budgets, cost drivers and financial performance.
  • Strengthening systems, processes and internal controls while looking for opportunities to improve efficiency and make better use of technology.
About you

You’ll be an experienced finance professional who enjoys being close to the numbers. This isn't a role where you delegate the detail and operate from above. You’ll need strong financial accounting capability, but also enjoy leading people, solving problems and understanding what is happening behind the numbers.

Ideally, you’ll bring:
  • A relevant tertiary qualification, with CA/CPA or equivalent preferred.
  • Strong financial accounting experience across month end, management reporting, reconciliations, budgeting, cashflow, audit and financial controls.
  • Previous experience leading, coaching and developing finance staff.
  • Experience within a multi-entity, contract funded, health, social services, public sector or similarly complex environment would be valuable.
  • Strong systems capability, ideally within an ERP environment. Dynamics 365 Business Central experience would be a bonus, not a deal breaker.
  • An analytical and inquisitive mindset - someone who spots when something doesn’t look right and is prepared to investigate why.
  • The ability to communicate financial information clearly to people who aren't accountants.
  • A collaborative, practical leadership style and a genuine willingness to embrace and contribute to the kaupapa of the organisation.

Most importantly, you’ll be someone who enjoys relationships. Effective finance partnering means getting away from your desk, talking with people, understanding their mahi and finding ways for finance to enable rather than create unnecessary barriers.

Benefits

This is an opportunity to join an organisation where your financial expertise contributes to something much bigger. You’ll also benefit from a workplace wellness programme and development opportunities.

Interested?

If you’re an experienced Finance Manager, Financial Accountant or senior finance professional ready to step into broader leadership, we’d love to hear from you. Apply online, or contact Jeanette Rendle at RWR Health for a confidential conversation. Ph 027 705 7079 or email: jeanetter@rwrhealth.co.nz

job.title: Community Physiotherapist
job.description:
The Opportunity

Our client is seeking an experienced Community Neuro Physiotherapist to join their Whangarei based interdisciplinary team.

This is not a sports concussion role. The work is meaningful, complex and grounded in real life. You’ll support clients recovering from car accidents, domestic violence, spinal injuries and traumatic brain injuries. The client group spans children through to older adults (85+), with a high Māori patient population and strong whānau involvement.

Rehabilitation is delivered in both clinic and community settings, and education forms a core part of the work. Much of your impact will come from your ability to clearly explain, coach and empower clients and their families as they navigate recovery.

This service is being intentional about finding the right person. Cultural fit, communication and genuine commitment matter just as much as clinical skill.
 
About the job
  • Deliver neuro-rehabilitation services across Northland
  • Manage a varied caseload including concussion, traumatic brain injury and spinal injuries
  • Work collaboratively within a strong interdisciplinary team
  • Provide education and support to clients and whānau
  • Balance autonomy with productivity expectations
  • Flexible hybrid working once established in the role
  • Monday to Friday, 40 hours per week within core working hours of 7.30am - 5.30pm 
What's on offer
  • Thorough induction and structured onboarding into your role
  • Ongoing professional development, supervision and internal education programmes
  • Support for external and postgraduate training
  • Reimbursement of Annual Practising Certificate
  • Strong, supportive team environment
  • Additional sick leave to support wellbeing
  • Salary aligned with Te Whatu Ora MECA $82,856 (step 2) to $107,600 (Step 7)
  • Access to exclusive staff discounts with major retailers
About you

You are a NZ Registered Physiotherapist (or eligible) with a current APC and driver’s licence. You will bring:

  • At least 2 years’ post graduate experience (community or neuro experience highly regarded)
  • Exceptional communication skills - able to educate, simplify complex information and build trust
  • Empathy, resilience and confidence working with vulnerable clients
  • Ability to balance compassion with productivity and accountability
  • A genuine interest in committing to Whangarei and building long-term client relationships
This role requires more than technical competence. It requires emotional intelligence, cultural humility and the ability to walk alongside clients during challenging stages of recovery.

Ready to take the next step?
If you're looking for a role where you can make a real difference, develop specialist skills and be supported by a values-driven team, we'd love to hear from you.
 
Apply now or reach out for a confidential discussion.
Contact Agency Director, Robbie McKenzie

job.title: Helpline Support Worker
job.description:
Do you have a passion for supporting rangatahi and want to make a meaningful impact through direct crisis intervention and clinical support? This is your opportunity to work with Youthline’s Helpline Services Team in a structured, high-impact role.

About the Role
As a Helpline Support Worker, you’ll be on the frontline providing essential support to young people accessing Youthline’s Helpline through text, phone, email, and webchat. You’ll also be a key support to Helpline Volunteers, providing mentoring, clinical guidance, and helping to manage risk in real-time.
This is a permanent, full-time role on a 4x4 roster (four days on, four days off).
  • Day shifts (6am–2:30pm) WFH
  • Afternoon shifts (2:00pm – 10:30pm)WFH
  • Evening shifts (6:00pm - Midnight) WFH
You’ll need to be confident in risk assessment, decision-making, and coaching others - often autonomously.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Deliver person-centred, strength-based support to Helpline clients
  • Provide clinical leadership and mentoring to Helpline Volunteers
  • Conduct and guide risk assessments and escalate as required
  • Maintain quality documentation and contribute to continuous improvement
  • Support a positive, inclusive, and safe team environment
What You’ll Bring:
  • Registration under the HPCA Act, NZAC, DAPAANZ, or SWRB
  • Experience in a mental health, counselling, or crisis support role
  • Strong risk assessment and clinical decision-making skills
  • Empathy, emotional regulation, and the ability to lead under pressure
  • Experience working in telehealth is highly desirable
What’s on Offer:
  • Work From Home! 
  • Fixed permanent role with good remuneration
  • The chance to make a direct impact on the wellbeing of rangatahi in Aotearoa
  • A strong clinical team culture with support and supervision
  • Work for a mission-driven organisation deeply rooted in community
This is a vital, rewarding position for someone who thrives in high-trust environments and believes in the power of connection, whanaungatanga, and youth-led support.

Apply Today!!
Or for a confidential discussion or to express your interest, please contact:
Robbie McKenzie
Director, RWR Health

job.title: Registered Psychologist Relocate to Timaru
job.description:
What's on offer
  • Salary of  $85,000-$105,000 , depending on experience
  • Full-time or part-time opportunities (minimum 15 hours per week)
  • 5 weeks annual leave
  • $2,500 annual professional development allowance
  • Up to $2,000 relocation assistance
  • Established caseload from day one
  • Low staff turnover and supportive team culture
  • Genuine multidisciplinary approach to client care
  • Opportunities to further develop your skills in concussion, pain management and complex psychological assessment
An exciting opportunity is available for a  Registered Psychologist or Clinical Psychologist  to join a well-established multidisciplinary rehabilitation provider in Timaru. Whether you're looking for full-time or part-time work (minimum 15 hours per week), you'll become part of a supportive team with an established caseload and strong clinical leadership.

This role offers meaningful work with clients recovering from a wide range of injuries, alongside excellent professional development and genuine work-life balance.

The Opportunity Working primarily within  ACC-funded rehabilitation , you'll support clients who have experienced traumatic injuries and require psychological assessment and intervention as part of their recovery.
Your caseload will include clients experiencing:
  • Chronic pain
  • Concussion and mild traumatic brain injury
  • Trauma following injury
  • Sensitive Claims
  • Mental health impacts of injury
  • Return-to-work and vocational rehabilitation needs
Every day is different. You'll manage your own diary and caseload, conducting psychological assessments, providing evidence-based therapy, preparing comprehensive reports, and working closely with a multidisciplinary team to help clients achieve the best possible outcomes.

Most assessments are completed from the Timaru clinic, with occasional home visits where reasonable adjustments are required.
About You We're looking for a Registered Psychologist or Clinical Psychologist who enjoys working collaboratively and is passionate about supporting people through recovery.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Registration (or eligibility for registration) with the New Zealand Psychologists Board
  • Around three years' or more post-registration experience
  • Strong psychological assessment and report writing skills
  • Experience working within rehabilitation, injury, or ACC environments
  • An interest or experience in pain management and concussion rehabilitation (highly desirable, but not essential)
Applications are also welcomed from overseas psychologists who are eligible to obtain New Zealand registration.
Why Join? You'll be joining a close-knit team with an excellent reputation for collaboration and staff retention. You'll work alongside experienced psychologists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, nurses, counsellors and administration staff, with support from an experienced Team Leader who understands the role firsthand.

If you're looking for a varied role where you can make a real difference while being supported by an experienced and collaborative team, we'd love to hear from you.

Know someone suitable? We offer a  $500 referral bonus  for successful referrals.

job.title: Family Violence Kaimahi
job.description:
About the organisation

Central Connect Whare Manaaki is a locally operated community agency that has supported the people of Central Hawke's Bay for more than 30 years.

Based in Waipukurau, the team provides free services including social work support and advocacy, counselling, Heartland Services and the CHB Foodbank.

At the heart of their work is walking alongside people and whānau through challenging times, building resilience and supporting their journey towards Mauri Ora - health and wellbeing. Guided by the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi, they provide a safe and confidential environment grounded in dignity, respect and manaakitanga.

About the job

This is a community facing position combining approximately 20 hours of coordination with 10 hours of direct family violence response including a small caseload. You will work with both those experiencing violence and those using violence and contribute to the organisation's aim of breaking intergenerational family cycles of trauma and harm. You will:
  • Coordinate the local Family Violence Interagency Response (FVIAR) table, where Police, Oranga Tamariki, iwi, health, mental health and community organisations come together to consider family violence reports and coordinate the best response for those involved.
  • Make contact with people following family violence incidents, often at a time when they may be overwhelmed, unsure of what they need or not yet ready to accept support.
  • Listen without judgement, assess immediate needs and risk, undertake safety planning and help connect people with the right services and support. 
  • Work 30 hours per week in total. Preferred working days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. There is some flexibility for the right person. Wednesday availability is particularly important.
About you
 
You must have experience working within family violence and a strong understanding of its dynamics. We're looking for someone who is:
  • Empathetic, grounded and genuinely non-judgemental
  • Experienced in family violence response
  • Confident completing risk assessments and safety planning
  • Able to establish rapport while maintaining strong professional boundaries
  • Comfortable having challenging conversations and engaging people who may initially reject support
  • Highly respectful of privacy and confidentiality
  • Able to work collaboratively across Police, government agencies, iwi and community providers
  • Practical, resilient and comfortable working with a high degree of autonomy
  • Committed to client centred, strengths based practice and supporting people to make their own choices
  • Skilled in using Microsoft Word, Outlook, Excel and client management software
Lived experience of family violence is not a barrier to appointment. However, due to the nature of this work, applicants with lived experience will need to have been free from a family violence relationship or environment for at least three years.
 
What is in it for you?
  • $32.50 per hour
  • External supervision
  • An opportunity to undertake meaningful work in the community you serve, alongside a small supportive team
  • Autonomy, professional support and the opportunity to make a very tangible difference for people at what can be one of the most difficult times in their lives.

job.title: Theatre Services Manager
job.description:
Some leadership roles are about fixing what is broken. 
This isn’t one of them.

This is an opportunity to step into a well established, high performing theatre service where the team is engaged, the culture is positive and the department is humming.

The current Theatre Services Manager has been promoted internally into the General Manager role - creating a rare opportunity to inherit a strong service with continuity, support and genuine momentum.

You’ll lead 7 operating theatres, 6 direct reports and approximately 65 staff across a diverse range of surgical specialties. Orthopaedics is a significant strength, with further growth underway across gynaecology, ophthalmology and robotic surgery.

New contracts have been secured. New surgeons are joining. A robotic surgery programme is developing. The foundations are firmly in place, and the opportunity now is to build on them.

A manager first. A clinician second.

There is considerable clinical expertise within this team. They don’t need someone to be the strongest clinician in every room - they need an experienced manager who can bring people, performance and operations together.

You’ll provide direction to an established group of theatre leaders, maintain strong relationships with surgeons and anaesthetists and ensure the service continues to deliver exceptional patient care while meeting its operational and commercial objectives.

This is a broad leadership role encompassing:
  • Theatre performance, utilisation and operational efficiency
  • Leadership and development of the perioperative team
  • Workforce planning, engagement and performance
  • Budget management and resource allocation
  • Quality, risk, infection prevention and health and safety
  • Strong relationships with surgeons, anaesthetists and internal stakeholders
  • Service development and delivery of future growth initiatives
You’ll report to a supportive General Manager who knows the service exceptionally well, having successfully led the theatre department herself. You’ll also join a collaborative and highly regarded senior leadership team.

Who will thrive here? You’ll be a credible perioperative leader who understands the unique demands of a busy theatre environment, but your real strength will be management. You’ll know how to empower capable clinical leaders, create clarity, make sound decisions and maintain high standards without needing to control every detail. You’ll be commercially aware, comfortable managing budgets and confident building trusted relationships with specialists and senior stakeholders.

You will also bring:
  • Current registration with the Nursing Council of New Zealand
  • At least five years’ experience as a Registered Nurse
  • A minimum of three years’ operating theatre experience
  • Previous people leadership and management experience
  • Experience managing budgets and stakeholder relationships
  • A sound understanding of New Zealand nursing legislation and theatre best practice
  • A collaborative, organised and resilient leadership style
What’s on offer? Alongside a salary of $160,000–$165,000, this role is eligible for a short-term performance incentive and includes:
  • Monday-to-Friday working hours
  • A strong and supportive leadership team
  • A genuinely positive and well-established team culture
  • Two insurance policies
  • Free onsite parking
  • Birthday leave
  • Long-service bonuses
  • Christmas shutdown period
  • Employee benefits, perks and discounts
  • Professional development and conference leave
For someone who wants the scale and professional challenge of leading a substantial surgical service, without inheriting a department in crisis, this is an exceptional opportunity!

The team is strong. The service is growing. The next chapter is ready to be led.

Apply through RWR Health or contact Jeanette Rendle, Agency Director ph 027 705 7079 for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Clinical Improvement Lead
job.description:
CLINICAL IMPROVEMENT LEAD | CLINICAL GOVERNANCE & QUALITY
Auckland Central | Youth Mental Health | Clinical Leadership

Lead clinical governance, quality improvement and risk frameworks for a nationally recognised organisation supporting young people across Aotearoa.

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

RWR Health is partnering with Youthline, a highly regarded national youth mental health and wellbeing organisation to appoint an experienced Clinical Improvement Lead.

This is an influential, organisation-wide position for a senior registered clinician who wants to shape clinical quality beyond an individual caseload. You will strengthen clinical governance, lead continuous improvement initiatives and provide trusted clinical advice across service delivery, organisational projects and strategic decision-making.

Working alongside executive leaders, service managers and clinical teams, you will help ensure clinical services remain safe, evidence-informed, responsive and aligned with professional standards.

With no direct reports. Its influence comes through clinical credibility, collaboration and the ability to turn governance and quality frameworks into meaningful improvements in practice.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
  • Leading the implementation, monitoring and ongoing development of the Clinical Governance Framework
  • Supporting or leading the Clinical Governance and Quality Committees
  • Reviewing clinical systems, processes and services to identify risks, gaps and opportunities for improvement
  • Developing and implementing practical quality and service-improvement initiatives
  • Providing senior clinical advice for complex, critical and high-risk situations
  • Strengthening clinical risk-assessment, escalation and incident-management processes
  • Advising on policy development, service design, funding applications and strategic projects
  • Monitoring clinical quality data, emerging risks, trends and improvement outcomes
  • Facilitating clinical meetings, reflective practice and professional-development activities
  • Developing training and resources across clinical governance, risk, quality and best practice
  • Building engagement with clinical governance and continuous improvement across the organisation
ABOUT YOU
You will be a credible and experienced clinician who can work comfortably across frontline practice, governance and organisational strategy. You will bring sound judgement, strong facilitation skills and the ability to influence people outside formal reporting lines.

You will ideally offer:
  • Significant clinical experience, including exposure to complex or high-risk environments
  • Experience in clinical governance, clinical quality, risk or continuous improvement
  • Experience developing, implementing or reviewing clinical frameworks and service-improvement initiatives
  • Strong leadership, facilitation and project-management capability
  • Confidence supporting complex clinical decisions and escalation processes
  • Strong knowledge of clinical, ethical, legislative and regulatory requirements
  • Excellent written communication, with the ability to contribute to policies, reports, funding applications and strategic initiatives
  • A collaborative, analytical and solutions-focused approach
  • Experience within youth, community, mental health or telehealth services would be highly valued
  • Knowledge and experience supporting Māori, Pacific, Rainbow, Asian and other priority communities would be advantageous
REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

You must hold a relevant tertiary clinical qualification and be fully registered with a recognised New Zealand professional or membership body under the HCPA Act such as SWRB, NZAC, NZNO, NZCCA, DAPAANZ or NZAP etc.

WHY CONSIDER THIS ROLE?

This is an opportunity to move beyond managing a single clinical service and contribute to quality and safety across an entire organisation.
You’ll have the scope to influence governance, policy, capability, service design and clinical decision-making while supporting an organisation with a strong purpose and a longstanding commitment to improving outcomes for rangatahi.

job.title: Clinical Quality & Project Specialist
job.description:
CLINICAL QUALITY & PROJECT SPECIALIST | YOUTH MENTAL HEALTH

ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY
Are you a registered mental health clinician who is naturally drawn to improving how services work, not just delivering them?

RWR Health is seeking a Clinical Quality & Project Specialist for Youthline, a  respected national youth mental health and wellbeing organisation based in Auckland Central.

This is a varied, hands-on position sitting between clinical practice, quality improvement and project delivery. You will review clinical practice, identify opportunities for improvement and help turn those insights into stronger policies, training, systems and services.

You will work closely with Helpline leadership, service managers, clinical teams and the wider Quality Improvement Team to support safe, consistent and evidence-informed care for rangatahi and other clients.

Unlike a purely administrative quality role, this position retains a connection to frontline service delivery. You will contribute to case management, clinical guidance and the nationwide 24/7 Helpline, including supporting occasional coverage requirements.

WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR
  • Reviewing and monitoring clinical practice against policy, procedure and best-practice standards
  • Identifying quality, training and service-development opportunities
  • Supporting clinical quality monitoring and governance processes
  • Helping services remain audit-ready through accurate and timely quality controls
  • Contributing to clinical incident reviews and improvement recommendations
  • Supporting the development and review of policies, procedures and clinical guidelines
  • Leading and supporting quality-improvement projects from design through to implementation and evaluation
  • Driving service innovation across Helpline, therapy and youth-development services
  • Contributing clinical expertise to workforce training and development
  • Supporting reflective practice, clinical debriefing and Helpline meetings
  • Contributing to case management and clear, person-centred care planning
  • Maintaining accurate clinical and quality information across client-management systems
  • Supporting the nationwide Helpline when required
ABOUT YOU

You will be an experienced, fully registered clinician who combines sound clinical judgement with curiosity about how services can be made safer, more consistent and more effective.
You will bring:
  • Proven mental health experience, ideally involving young people and whānau
  • Demonstrated quality-improvement or service-development experience
  • The ability to translate research and evidence into practical clinical improvements
  • Confidence identifying and prioritising clinical risk
  • The ability to make timely, sound decisions using best-practice clinical standards
  • Experience engaging clients, families, whānau and community stakeholders
  • Strong reflective practice and a calm, non-judgemental approach
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Confidence managing competing priorities in a responsive service environment
  • The ability to lead, coach, provide feedback and support workforce development
  • A genuine commitment to improving outcomes for young people
  • Telehealth, Helpline or crisis-service experience would be advantageous
REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS
To be considered, you must hold a current Annual Practising Certificate and be fully registered in New Zealand as one of the following:
  • A health practitioner registered under the HPCA Act, such as a nurse, psychologist, psychotherapist or occupational therapist etc.
  • A registered alcohol and drug or gambling practitioner with DAPAANZ
  • A fully registered social worker
  • A counsellor fully registered with NZAC
You must also have relevant clinical experience within mental health, ideally including youth mental health or addiction services.

WHY THIS ROLE?
This position offers a rare combination of direct clinical connection and broader organisational impact.
You will be able to see what is happening in practice, identify what could work better and then help design and implement the solution. Your work will influence clinical quality, workforce capability, service innovation and the experience of rangatahi accessing support.

job.title: Pharmacy Manager
job.description:
Pharmacy Team Lead | Invercargill
A fantastic opportunity for an experienced Pharmacist or someone ready to take the next step into leadership.

Are you an experienced Pharmacist looking for your next challenge? Or are you ready to step up from a Pharmacist role into a position where you can develop your leadership and management skills?

We're recruiting on behalf of a well-established national pharmacy group seeking a Pharmacy Team Lead to join its busy Invercargill community pharmacy.

Newly graduated Pharmacists are also encouraged to apply, alongside experienced Pharmacists and those already working in leadership positions. Previous Pharmacy Manager experience is not essential — what matters most is your motivation, people skills and willingness to grow.

This is an opportunity to combine your clinical expertise with leadership, helping to develop a strong team while delivering exceptional patient care.

The Opportunity
This is a replacement position within a busy, high-performing community pharmacy with an established customer base and an exciting opportunity for its next chapter.
As Pharmacy Team Lead, you'll play an important role in supporting the pharmacy team, developing people and helping create a positive, collaborative and high-performing workplace culture.
Initially, the role will involve approximately 80% dispensing and 20% leadership/management, with the opportunity for the leadership component to increase as the team continues to develop.
You'll have the opportunity to make a genuine impact across the pharmacy while continuing to use your clinical skills and developing your leadership capability.

About the Role
As Pharmacy Team Lead, you'll be responsible for:
  • Leading, mentoring and developing your pharmacy team
  • Supporting staff performance, development and regular reviews
  • Building a positive, collaborative and high-performing culture
  • Supporting pharmacy sales and business performance
  • Managing both personal and pharmacy-wide KPIs
  • Delivering safe and accurate dispensing services
  • Ensuring compliance with all pharmacy legislation, professional standards and operating procedures
  • Supporting health initiatives and preventative healthcare services
  • Building strong relationships with customers, healthcare professionals and the wider store leadership team
  • Identifying opportunities to improve pharmacy services and patient care
The Team
You'll be joining an established pharmacy team currently consisting of:
  • 2 Pharmacists
  • 2 Dispensing Technicians
  • 1 Pharmacy Assistant
The pharmacy is continuing to build its permanent team, creating an exciting opportunity for the Pharmacy Team Lead to contribute to team development and future growth.
You'll also have strong support from experienced pharmacy professionals and the wider leadership team.

A Busy Community Pharmacy
This is a high-volume pharmacy with strong prescription numbers and a loyal customer base.

Services currently include:
  • Vaccinations
  • Influenza vaccinations
  • COVID-19 boosters
  • Medicines Use Reviews
  • Free blister packing
  • Shingrix
  • Priorix
  • Gardasil 9
  • Bexsero
  • MenQuadfi
The pharmacy does not provide Methadone or Clozapine services.
The local community includes a large Vietnamese population alongside English-speaking customers, so you'll be comfortable communicating with people from diverse backgrounds and using translation devices where required.

About You
We're looking for a Pharmacist who is motivated to grow, develop and take ownership.
You'll bring:
  • Current New Zealand Pharmacist registration and APC
  • Community pharmacy experience
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • A collaborative and positive approach
  • A willingness to develop your leadership capability
  • The ability to take initiative and work confidently
  • An interest in commercial and operational aspects of pharmacy
  • A genuine commitment to customer care
What's on Offer
  • $113,000–$133,000 salary depending on experience
  • Employee share scheme
  • Up to $7,500 relocation assistance
  • Monday–Friday, 9am–6pm
  • No weekend work
  • Opportunity to work a 4-day week
  • Four weeks annual leave
  • Ten days sick leave
  • No probation period
  • Strong leadership support
  • Ongoing career development
Please note that while relocation assistance is available, visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
